Which of the given points lie on the line $y=-5x+6?$
sources.worked_solution:
The plotted points correspond to the $xy$-pairs $A(0,5),B(1,2)$ and $C(2,-4).$

To check whether a point lies on the line, we substitute the coordinates of the point into the equation and determine whether the resulting statement is true.

- Substituting the point $A(0,5)$ results in a false statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x+6 \\ (5) & =-5(0)+6 \\ 5 & =6\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $A$ does *not* lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $B(1,2)$ results in a false statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x+6 \\ (2) & =-5(1)+6 \\ 2 & =1\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $B$ does not lie on the line.

- Substituting the point $C(2,-4)$ results in a true statement:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x+6 \\ (-4) & =-5(2)+6 \\ -4 & =-4\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $C$ does lie on the line.

Finally, only point $C$ lies on the line.
